sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: gRPC interview questions cover the high-performance RPC framework increasingly common in microservice interviews — Protocol Buffers (proto3), the four service types (unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, bidi), interceptors, deadlines and cancellation, load balancing, gRPC vs REST vs messaging trade-offs, and the gRPC + Spring Boot integration patterns. This page is the one to use for any role that mentions internal service-to-service RPC at scale.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
gRPC = **HTTP/2 + Protocol Buffers + 4 RPC styles** (unary / server-stream / client-stream / bidi).

- **Codegen** from `.proto` keeps client and server contract-locked.
- **Deadlines** propagate through the call chain — set them.
- **Interceptors** for auth, logging, metrics — both client and server side.
- **Load-balancing** — client-side (look-aside) common in service meshes.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Grpc fundamentals** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Protobuf field numbers** are immutable — never reuse, even after delete.
- **Backwards compatibility** — add new optional fields, never repurpose.
- **Browser support** — gRPC-Web is required; pure gRPC won't work from a browser.
- **Error codes** — gRPC status codes ≠ HTTP; learn the mapping.
- **vs REST** — pick gRPC for internal service-to-service, REST for external APIs.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd define the contract in proto, version fields by adding new tags only, set deadlines per call, route through a service mesh for client-side LB, and reserve REST for the external edge where browser + caching matter."*
